reference.title: Dumbbell Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold the brace on the way down, breathe out as you stand.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short pause, 1.6 s up

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell held in the hand opposite the standing leg; stop about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2)
prescription.progression: Add load, then add a pause at the bottom

cues.text: Stand on the right leg, knee soft, dumbbell in the left hand, left foot just off the floor.
Hinge at the right hip: the chest goes down as the left leg reaches back, one straight line from head to heel.
Stop when the trunk is about level or the hamstring is stretched; hips stay square to the floor.
Drive the right hip forward and stand tall, bringing the free leg under you.
Balance tall on the right leg for a breath, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the hips (the free hip rotates up toward the ceiling)
mistakes.fix: Point the free toes at the floor and keep both hip bones level.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach lower
mistakes.fix: Stop where the back is still flat; the range comes from the standing hip.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the standing knee into a squat
mistakes.fix: Keep a small, steady knee bend and push the hips back.
Slow down; touch a wall or rack lightly with the free hand if needed.

kinematics.norm: Hinge until the trunk is about level, the free leg in line with it (clinical opinion)
Standing knee softly bent, about 15-25 degrees, nearly constant (clinical opinion)
Extends back in line with the trunk, toes pointing down, pelvis square (clinical opinion)
Dumbbell in the hand opposite the standing leg gave higher gluteus maximus and erector spinae activity than the same-side hand (Mo 2023)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #975212, Dumbbell Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (male), video (movement reference)

Mo, Ngai, Ng, Sin, Luk & Ho 2023, effects of loading positions on the activation of trunk and hip muscles during flywheel and dumbbell single-leg Romanian deadlift exercises (Front Physiol 14:1264604)
McAllister, Hammond, Schilling, Ferreria, Reed & Weiss 2014, muscle activation during various hamstring exercises (J Strength Cond Res 28(6):1573-1580)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Balance: practise near a wall or rack; set the free foot down whenever you need to.
Low-back pain: shorten the range and keep the spine neutral.
modify: Poor balance: keep the free toes lightly on the floor behind you (kickstand RDL).
Tight hamstrings: stop higher and bend the standing knee a little more.
regressions: Bodyweight single-leg RDL holding a wall.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor of the standing leg. Superior gluteus maximus reached very high activity (about 105-169% MVIC) in the dumbbell and flywheel single-leg RDLs of Mo 2023, highest with the load in the opposite hand.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen as the hips hinge back over the standing leg, then extend the hip; biceps femoris was about 70-122% MVIC in Mo 2023.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the standing hip.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat from head to free heel; erector spinae were highly active, more so with the contralateral load (Mo 2023).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back flat from head to free heel; erector spinae were highly active, more so with the contralateral load (Mo 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level over the standing leg (about 41-89% MVIC in Mo 2023).
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the trunk does not twist toward the dumbbell.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist rotation from the one-sided load; external oblique activity was only low to moderate (Mo 2023).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist rotation from the one-sided load; external oblique activity was only low to moderate (Mo 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Lifts the free leg back in line with the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the dumbbell arm close to the body.
